chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Dhubyan from Musa ibn Uqayl from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Umar ibn Hanzalah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man sold a piece of land on the condition that it contained ten ajribah (units of land). The buyer purchased it from him with its boundaries, paid the price, and the sale was concluded, and they parted. When he measured the land, he found it to be only five ajribah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he wishes, he may reclaim his money and take back the land. If he wishes, he may return the land and keep all his money. Unless there are also lands of his adjacent to that land, in which case he should compensate him (the buyer) for the adjacent land, and the sale becomes binding upon him, and he must fulfill the sale in its entirety. If he has no other land in that place besides the one he sold, then if the buyer wishes, he may take the land and reclaim the surplus of his money, and if he wishes, he may return the land and take all the money.'

key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَجْرِبَةٍ: ten ajribah (a unit of land measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the options for a buyer if the land purchased by measurement turns out to be smaller than specified?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *khiyar al-ghabn* (option of deficiency) in sales by measure, emphasizing fairness when the exact quantity is unknown at the time of contract. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the seller's right to rectify the discrepancy by adding adjacent land or refunding the value, ensuring the buyer receives the full agreed-upon quantity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic focus on preventing *gharar* (uncertainty) and ensuring equitable exchange in commercial transactions.
